nodes.name: NiOx@BCNTs Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: In the typical synthesis of NiOx@BCNTs, 1.11 g of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O was first dissolved in an appropriate amount of deionized water. Then, 20 g of melamine was added into the above solution. The water completely evaporated in an 80°C oil bath with magnetic stirring. Afterward, the mixture was ground into powder, and transferred into a 30 mL crucible. The solid mixture experienced two sections of the temperature program: First the material was heated to 600°C for 1 h, and the temperature further rose to 700°C for 2 h in a muffle furnace in N2 flow (400 mL min⁻¹). Finally, the products were cooled down to room temperature, and NiOx@BCNTs was obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows bamboo-like carbon nanotubes with diameters 10-20 nm containing Ni-based nanoparticles with mean size of 12.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The as-synthesized CNTs had diameters ranging from 10 to 20 nm (Figure 1b). The histogram in Figure 1a provides evidence for the Ni-based NPs with a mean size of 12.5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals well-defined lattice fringes consistent with (111) and (200) facets of Ni⁰ crystal and unique Ni/NiO interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As Figure 1d revealed, an encapsulated Ni NP sample with well-defined lattice fringes was consistent with the (111) and (200) facet of the Ni⁰ crystal. ... It is worth mentioning that the unique interface of Ni/NiO dwelled in the hybrids (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of graphite-type lattice (C, PDF 41-1487) and Ni/NiO (Ni, PDF 65-2865, NiO, PDF 65-5745).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Characteristic peaks of both the graphite-type lattice (C, PDF 41-1487) and Ni/NiO (Ni, PDF 65-2865, NiO, PDF 65-5745) were recorded.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows peaks at 870.2 and 853.0 eV corresponding to Ni⁰ (36.2% content) and remaining peaks assigned to NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2b, the peaks centering at 870.2 and 853.0 eV corresponded to the position of Ni⁰, and the rest of the peaks are assigned to the form of NiO. ... the content of Ni⁰ in NiO_x@BCNTs (36.2%)

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows D-, G-bands and 2D peak of carbon with high I_D/I_G indicating structural defects from N dopants.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Not only were typical D- and G-bands of carbon seen, but also a well-defined 2D peak (Figure 2c) was observed. The high I_D/I_G value indicated more structural defects...

nodes.characterization_summary: BET method shows specific surface area of 314 m²/g from N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms (type IV, mesoporous).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The conventional Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) method was employed to calculate the specific surface area. ... The N₂ adsorption isotherm measured for NiO_x@BCNTs resembled type IV with a large specific surface area (314 m² g⁻¹) and mesoporous feature

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines nickel content of NiO_x@BCNTs as 39.74 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the ICP-AES result revealed, the nickel content of NiO_x@BCNTs was 39.74 wt%.

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-TPR shows NiO reduction starts at 400°C and completes at 850°C with no carbon decomposition peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the TPR results (Figure 5a), NiO started to be reduced at 400°C, and could be thoroughly reduced at 850°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl of 38.8 mF cm⁻² indicates high ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NiO_x@BCNTs displayed a large double-layer capacitance (C_dl) of 38.8 mF cm⁻².
